operations.description:
Submit a new administrator privilege request.

This operation allows authenticated member users to apply for administrator privileges by submitting a formal request. The request requires a detailed reason explaining the user's qualifications, motivations, and how they plan to contribute to platform governance. The reason field corresponds to the 'reason' column in the discussion_board_admin_requests table which records the member's justification for seeking administrative role. Upon submission, the request enters a pending status (stored in the 'status' column) awaiting review by super administrators.

The system validates that the user does not have any existing pending requests and ensures the request reason meets content guidelines including non-whitespace validation. Additionally, the system confirms the member is not currently banned and validates the reason text contains meaningful content. The 'created_at' timestamp is automatically generated upon successful submission. Once submitted, the request becomes visible to super administrators for review and cannot be modified by the requesting user. This operation supports the community governance framework by providing a formal pathway for user progression to administrative roles.

Security considerations include rate limiting to prevent abuse and logging all submission activities for audit purposes. Users must be in good standing (not banned) to submit requests, and duplicate pending requests from the same user are automatically rejected. The operation creates records in the discussion_board_admin_requests table with fields: id (primary UUID), discussion_board_member_id (foreign key to member), reason, status, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at (for soft deletion).

This operation provides super administrators with the ability to audit and review administrator assignment actions performed by regular members within the platform. The search functionality supports filtering by various criteria including the member who performed the assignment, assignment type (promotion/demotion/initial/system), date ranges, and role transitions involved.

The response includes paginated summary information showing each assignment's essential details such as the roles involved, assignment type, reason provided, and timestamps. This enables effective oversight of the administrator assignment process and ensures transparency in platform governance decisions.

Super administrators can use this operation to monitor assignment patterns, verify compliance with platform policies, and maintain accountability for role transitions within the community. The search capabilities support both broad overviews and targeted investigations based on specific criteria.

This operation provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for tracking administrator role transitions including promotions, demotions, and initial assignments. The attachment's relationship to its parent article is validated through the article_id foreign key to ensure proper access control and data integrity.

Security considerations require verifying that users have appropriate permissions to view the parent article before accessing its attachments. The operation follows standard REST patterns for resource retrieval and provides all necessary information for client applications to handle file downloads and display attachment details appropriately.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a specific file attachment from an article.

This operation deletes both the physical file from storage and the attachment metadata record from the database. Only the article author or administrators with appropriate privileges can perform this operation. The deletion is irreversible and removes all traces of the attachment from the system.

When an attachment is deleted, the file is immediately removed from storage and the attachment record is marked as deleted. This operation follows the cascade deletion pattern defined in the database schema where attachments are dependent on their parent articles. Users should exercise caution when deleting attachments as this action cannot be undone.

The operation requires valid article and attachment identifiers and proper authorization. If the user lacks permission or the resources cannot be found, appropriate error responses will be returned. Administrators can delete attachments from any article regardless of ownership, while regular users can only delete attachments from articles they authored.

This operation provides technical information from the discussion_board_image_attachments table including pixel dimensions (width, height), accessibility alt text, and camera EXIF data when available from discussion_board_image_attachment_exif_data. The metadata helps client applications optimize image display, provide accessibility features, and present photographic context to users.

Image dimensions (width and height in pixels from discussion_board_image_attachments) enable responsive layout calculations and proper aspect ratio preservation. Alt text supports screen readers and improves accessibility compliance. EXIF camera data includes manufacturer information, exposure settings, and GPS coordinates from discussion_board_image_attachment_exif_data when present, providing valuable context about image creation.

Security considerations: Users must have appropriate permissions to view the parent article through the discussion_board_articles table. Image metadata is accessible to anyone who can view the article, as it contains technical information rather than sensitive content. The operation validates that the attachment belongs to the specified article via the article_id foreign key in discussion_board_attachments before returning metadata.

Related operations: Use GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/attachments to list all attachments for an article, including image attachments. This operation provides detailed technical metadata for a specific image attachment identified by its UUID.

page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The

the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.

records.description:

essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render

alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
